key_insight: Adding biofouling to a 3-D global Eulerian microplastic model shows that surface-clean particles can sink, disperse, and re-enter transport pathways, strongly reshaping large-microplastic distributions.
engineering_relevance: Including time-evolving particle properties in Eulerian transport models improves prediction of microplastic accumulation zones and vertical exposure pathways, which is important for ocean monitoring and cleanup planning.
method: Augmented the Eulerian concentration field with a new dimension for biomass attachment density on microplastic surfaces.
Coupled microplastic transport with biofouling-driven changes in buoyancy and vertical motion in a 3-D global model.
Compared idealized and global simulations across particle sizes to isolate when biofouling changes transport behavior.
evidence_signal: Against a global trawler dataset, adding biofouling reduced outlying model-observation points from 25% to 13%, indicating better agreement with observations.
watch_item: The effect depends on particles being initially buoyant and on local plankton growth exceeding decay, so the improvement may not generalize to all ocean regions or microplastic types.
paper_title: Effect of Biofouling on Microplastic Transport in a 3-D Global Eulerian Model
